title: Schema Validator
description: Build a runtime validation library with composable schemas, custom error messages, and nested validation.

steps.title: Implement String and Number Validators
steps.description: Create `string()` and `number()` schema factories. Each returns an object with a `parse(input)` method that returns `{success, data, error}`. `string()` validates typeof === 'string'. `number()` validates typeof === 'number'. Print `'Valid: value'` on success and `'Error: message'` on failure.
hints: Return a schema object with a `parse` method that checks the type
Use `{success: true, data: input}` for valid and `{success: false, error: '...'}` for invalid
Include the input value in the error message for clarity

verification.successMessage: String and number validators correctly validate type
verification.failureMessage: Base validators did not produce expected output

steps.title: Add Object Schema with Property Validation
steps.description: Create an `object(schema)` factory that takes a shape definition like `{name: string(), age: number()}`. The `parse` method validates each property against its schema. Return detailed errors per property. Print the validated object on success or the first error on failure.
hints: Iterate over the shape keys and call each schema's parse method
Collect errors in an object keyed by property path
A valid parse should return the original input object as data

verification.successMessage: Object schema validates all properties correctly
verification.failureMessage: Object schema did not validate properties

steps.title: Implement Array and Nested Validation
steps.description: Create an `array(itemSchema)` factory that validates each element of an array against `itemSchema`. Support nested objects: `object({items: array(object({id: number()}))})`. Print nested validation results with a tree-like indentation of valid/invalid paths.
hints: Use a helper function that tracks the current path as an array of keys
For arrays, validate every element and collect element-level errors
Format the output to show path chains like `items[0].id`

verification.successMessage: Array and nested validation works with path tracking
verification.failureMessage: Nested validation did not produce path-aware output

steps.title: Add Optional and Default Values
steps.description: Add `.optional()` modifier that allows `undefined` values and `.default(value)` modifier that substitutes a default when the value is `undefined`. Chain these after any schema: `string().optional()`, `number().default(0)`. Print the final parsed value with defaults applied.
hints: Wrap the existing parse to check for undefined before delegating
Store modifiers as properties on the schema object
Apply default before running the type check

verification.successMessage: Optional and default modifiers work correctly
verification.failureMessage: Optional or default values were not applied

steps.title: Build Custom Validators
steps.description: Add a `.refine(fn, message)` method to schemas that runs a custom validation function after type checks. The refine function receives the parsed value and returns `true/false`. On failure, use `message` as the error. Print custom error messages from refinements.
hints: Wrap the existing parse pipeline — run type check first, then refine
Store refinements in an array on the schema (multiple refinements allowed)
The error message from refine should include both the custom message and the value

verification.successMessage: Custom refinement validators produce custom error messages
verification.failureMessage: Refinement validation did not produce the expected error

steps.title: Implement Union and Intersection Types
steps.description: Create `or(schemaA, schemaB)` (union) that passes if either schema passes, trying A first. Create `and(schemaA, schemaB)` (intersection) that passes only if both pass, merging the results. Print which schema branch matched for unions and merged errors for intersections.
hints: For `or`, try schemaA first; if it fails, try schemaB; if both fail, combine errors
For `and`, run both schemas and collect all errors if either fails
Unions should report which branch succeeded: 'Matched: branch A'

verification.successMessage: Union and intersection combinators work correctly
verification.failureMessage: Schema combinators did not produce the expected output

steps.title: Add Formatted Error Messages
steps.description: Improve error reporting to produce a full error tree. When validation fails, show the path (e.g., `users[1].address.zip`), the expected type, the received value, and any refinement errors. Print the complete error tree as a formatted multi-line string.
hints: Collect path segments in an array and join them with dots and brackets
Include both expected and actual types in error leaves
Use recursion to build a nested error object before printing

verification.successMessage: Formatted error tree shows path, expected, and received values
verification.failureMessage: Error tree output is missing key fields
